summary: Okanogan County lookout above the Methow Valley. A 1923 cupola cabin was replaced in 1950 by the current L-4; full-time staffing ended around 2014 and it is now on call.

facts.design: Current L-4 cab with catwalk on a 15' timber tower (1950), replacing an original D-6 cupola cabin (1923)

access.note: Reached on foot. Sources read do not say whether visitors may enter the cab; it remains a working fire lookout.

visit.trail_note: Hike from Early Winters campground. WTA lists 3.7 miles round trip; OutdoorsNW says 3.5 miles. WTA lists the America the Beautiful Pass or Northwest Forest Pass as the parking pass.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says staffed every year since 1923. OutdoorsNW says regular staffing ended in 2015; WTA ties the change to 2014, when the staffer moved to Leecher. Read as a change over time; the newer accounts are used for current status.
The register gives 6,737 ft (2,053 m), which matches the record. Firelookout.com gives 7001 ft and WTA says about 7,000 ft. Not reconciled; the register figure is used.
WTA gives 3.7 miles round trip; OutdoorsNW gives 3.5 miles. Both are shown in the story.

sources.title: Fire Tower Lookouts of the Okanogan

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 27.0 is not supported by any page read. The register and firelookout.com give a '15' timber' tower, which may mean tower height or cab size, so no height was written. Forest name: the register says Okanogan National Forest; the current name was not confirmed in a page read. Staffing status is undated (WTA). Lightning Bill spelling varies: WTA uses 'Lightning Bill'; OutdoorsNW writes 'Lighting Bill'. A 2023 Cascadia Daily News item (search snippet only, not read) reportedly says the lookout has been back in use since 2021; not used. Page reads for this lookout: five.
